title: A weapon is four meshes of two kinds, not one box
note: The weapon is at least four meshes of two geometry types (body, barrel, grip, sight) or a modelled asset; one box is not a gun.
intent: A single box in the corner of the screen is read as a placeholder within one frame. Build the weapon from a body, a cylindrical barrel, a grip angled back from the body, and a sight or rail on top, at minimum — four meshes of at least two geometry families, which is what makes a silhouette. Keep it in real proportions against the hands, and put the muzzle where the barrel ends. A mesh modelled in Blender and loaded with loadAsset counts as built from parts.

check.js: meshes('weapon').some(m => m.userData && m.userData.asset) || (meshes('weapon').length >= 4 && new Set(meshes('weapon').map(m => m.geometry && m.geometry.type)).size >= 2)
check.note: The weapon is built from at least 4 meshes of at least 2 geometry types (body, barrel, grip, sight…) — one box is a primitive, not a gun. A modelled asset (userData.asset from src/assets.js) counts as built from parts.

port: The weapon facet returns one group with named children (body, barrel, grip, sight, muzzle) so the muzzle and sight checks have something to find.
